# Stellar Discovery Trust Layer

**TokenJunkieLabs — SCF #46 Build / Open Track**

Concise nine-answer working edition, 13 October 2026. The funding case is contained in these answers; the complete canonical manuscript, source index, budget and finance companion remain available for editing and engineering inspection. The existing submission workspace will apply the issuer's actual field labels and limits when the invitation arrives.

## Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs builds open-source, self-hostable software for selling useful APIs, datasets and agent operations on Stellar. A buyer approves a defined task and price, pays, and receives the complete result in an application it can continue using. The merchant retains the corresponding fulfillment and accounting. Another engineer can receive the installation and continue its customer work.

We request **$38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance**. The outcome is **two independently operated merchant services and two independent buyer operators**: one complete approved testnet purchase per merchant by day 30; recurring testnet use and the same useful service through two independent facilitators by day 90; and maintainable mainnet services with returning buyers by day 150.

The working product supplies the foundation. Funding develops the remaining source and consumer adaptations, Stellar deployment, provider compatibility, monitoring and recovery for those two services. Reusable improvements return to the public product. The six packages below fund prospective installation work; the broader catalog remains existing development.

## Customer problem, need and adoption

Our initial customer is a recurring API or data-service operator, or an agency implementing it in a customer's application. The commissioning payer buys installation and handover; the merchant receives resource payments; the buyer purchases useful output. Their workorder identifies each role and its authority.

Payment alone does not tell an analyst whether every agreed page arrived, the reporting period and units survived, or the result is usable. An agent task may require several paid calls under one spending limit. If settlement succeeds before an interrupted response, the buyer needs recovery through the existing entitlement or delivery session, and the merchant needs a clear fulfillment outcome.

|Selected installation pattern|Useful buyer output|Reason to return|
| --- | --- | --- |
|Economic or operational reporting|A complete report and selected underlying data with original units, period, source edition and review decisions.|The next required reporting period or a materially revised source edition.|
|Typed queries or refreshed datasets|Every agreed paid page/file with the query, population, aggregate price and merchant fulfillment.|A distinct needed query or source refresh used in the continuing buyer application.|

The two funded installations remain to be selected. Veridex invited the buyer CLI into its testnet cohort and reported no third-party testing budget. CoCart's founder asked who introduces customers, pays and contracts for implementation. Blockscout expressed interest and reported no integration budget; Nansen declined. These conversations clarify the commercial route. The completed product demonstrates delivery capability; independent adoption is the funded outcome.

Before funded development starts, each existing installation workorder will name its independently controlled merchant and buyer, commissioning payer, authorized source, host, receiving engineer and acceptance owner. It will fix the useful task, population/period, complete output, advertised paid unit, spending cap, cost owner and remaining changes assigned to the six packages. Customer selection and access preparation therefore precede day 1 engineering. Actual selection and agreement states remain visible.

The thirty-purchase T3 target requires recurring demand: two buyers buying once per ordinary weekday produce only twenty purchases in fourteen days. Selected jobs must support at least thirty distinct useful paid requests across both buyers and merchants during the target window. Multiple advertised pages may be necessary for one task; artificial splitting, retries and saved-result reopens do not create demand or extra purchases.

The commercial offer is implementation and handover followed by separately scoped care. Merchants retain resource receipts; partners retain customer relationships. Workorders set acceptance, included corrections, responsibilities and payment terms. Grant and paid customer work allocate each engineering change and hour once.

## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar supplies purchase authorization and settlement. In the existing x402 Exact flow, the buyer signs a Soroban token-transfer authorization binding payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiry; the selected facilitator submits it on the reviewed network. An explicit sponsorship policy can cover fees. We use existing Stellar SDKs and token contracts.

Our contribution connects that payment to the complete customer task: the approved HTTP method/endpoint or MCP tool/arguments, source edition, scope, aggregate spending, every agreed output, fulfillment and accounting. The buyer retains signing/spending authority; the merchant retains source, pricing and fulfillment authority.

Stellar x402 libraries provide challenges, authorization and signed retries; the Stellar CLI supplies signing identity. Facilitators verify and settle, Bazaar describes resources, ApiCharge provides typed paid access and retained service levels, and MPP Router provides paid proxy access, response caching and job polling. The proposed Open Track value builds on these foundations: a reusable customer workflow that remains usable across multiple calls, interrupted delivery, source change and independent handover. The funded installations develop and publish the adaptations needed for recurring independent use.

Two-facilitator acceptance uses the **same useful service**, holding schema, population and output constant. The retained Vellar/Periplo comparison found no shared seller/route identity; T2 therefore includes actual registration and wire/payment/fee-policy compatibility. Existing catalog entries are not substituted for that deployment.

The submitted selection remains Open Track, subject to issuer invitation and review. No new token, domestic payment rail or fiat on/off-ramp is proposed.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

|Component|Responsibility|
| --- | --- |
|Merchant workspace|Select authorized source/query, output schema, price and limits; review changes and withdrawals.|
|HTTP or MCP resource|Preserve types, nulls, keys, pagination, units, period and snapshot/live meaning; use authorized credential references.|
|Buyer approval and budget|Retain the exact method/tool, inputs, scope and payment option; check challenge/schema before signing; reserve aggregate task spending and enforce per-payment limits.|
|Stellar settlement|Retain network, asset, payer, recipient, atomic amount, expiry and fee policy; independently reconcile the transfer through RPC.|
|Delivery and accounting|Receive all agreed output; retain original attempts, fulfillment and acknowledgment; separate principal, fees, invoices and receipts.|
|Recovery and receiving|Reconcile original dispatch after uncertain responses; restore source, configuration, customer files and history for the receiving engineer.|

Saved intents support execution, history and complete downloads. A prepaid call retains its original selected pass and consumed allowance when defaults change. MPP Charge retains its own challenge and recovery lifecycle. An uncertain transfer is reconciled before further payment action; a settled purchase with unfinished output continues its existing entitlement or delivery session.

Node.js supplies browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces, alongside Python/SQLite and PHP/WordPress/WooCommerce applications. Releases identify source, upstream SDK/contract versions and licenses; any funded contract modifications will be published under compatible open-source terms.

The current product implements the components above; the funded work adapts and operates them for the selected independent customers. T1 joins the selected sources, consumers and operator authority; T2 implements actual provider compatibility and monitored recovery; T3 delivers mainnet recurring use and independent maintenance. The unified [development guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/68929767fd9c138e3bcee2df65ea9e5928ca565a/products/merchant-workspace/DEVELOPMENT.md) and complete [financial walkthrough](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/2d1854f4b148b41d8c96bc0f8de2924faa2a8f84/stellar-forge/developer-site/dist/grant-data/financial-walkthrough.md) describe the same operating product and customer accounts.

## Working product and demonstrated results

The baseline is **18 distinct team-operated testnet purchases totaling 411,000 stroops / 0.0411 native XLM**, with fees separate. Independent customer adoption and mainnet use are the next funded outcomes.

|Operated example|Observed useful result|
| --- | --- |
|Complete paid HPD acquisition|Two 10,000-stroop purchases returned 100 + 44 rows: one complete 144-row Queens HPD task, reopened as CSV/JSONL with source and accounting.|
|Limited query and product/team film|One 50,000-stroop purchase returned 100 rows, 14 columns and 53,468 bytes, with truncation explicitly true. It reopened with signing disconnected and in another directory. The film is 3:32.|
|Recurring data and analytical receiving|All 830 original OData Orders passed through typed collection, saved SQL, report, two-sheet workbook and independent receiving. Three subscription editions, original-request replay and publisher/customer restores completed; the unchanged source produced zero row changes.|
|Staff, billing and handover|Six profiles, three work records and two example invoices completed contribution, review, payment and correction across fifteen desktop/mobile views with zero errors. Cold receiving retained all 421 source files and history. A separate complete 243-file billing application reopened two planning cases; its $4,400 Paid and subsequent $4,400 Open examples retain their example identity.|

Saved-pass operations preserved original pass selection and consumed allowance after default changes, shutdown and cold receiving. OpenLineage receiving preserved the 1,000-row measurement, its decision against a 1,001-row requirement, unknown unreported column count and two matching 76-file exports.

Catalog discovery was measured separately: 27 HTTP resources, 33 queries and 31 scored query–resource pairs. Declared-resource retrieval improved 22→31 and top-three placement 19→29; eleven positions improved and twenty were unchanged. Direct/indexed results agreed for all 33 queries. Nine general queries have no expected-resource mapping.

The [3:32 product/team film](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/releases/download/scf-presentation-20261011/stellar-forge-scf46-presentation.mp4) leads into the existing buyer reviewer: inspect scope, read the complete retained result, follow its original purchase/accounting, export the closed Buyer and receive it independently. This uses the original payment and historical source. The film's limited 100-row response and the separate complete 144-row acquisition remain distinct.

## Threat response and outcome measurement

T2 binds the existing ten threat decisions and eight monitoring/response definitions to the actual installations: source/release, authority, network/facilitator, protected records, signals, numerical thresholds, notification/acknowledgment routes and primary/backup responders. It covers altered offers/approvals, payment/output attribution, unauthorized access, interrupted fulfillment, missing observations and restoration of the wrong generation.

The merchant owns source, terms and fulfillment; the buyer owns signing and aggregate spending; the facilitator owns its service and fee policy. The receiving engineer gets the selected release, protected state and open cases. The two required recovery exercises retain financial and delivery states, response/recovery time, useful output and observation gaps, then reopen that history after restart.

A **completed purchase** has one distinct approved intent, independently observed native transfer and complete useful accepted output. Transactions are deduplicated per network; assets/fees stay separate. A prepaid pass counts once after its first agreed operation produces accepted output; later calls are usage. A **completed customer task** requires every agreed page/file or order action. The 144-row example therefore has two purchases and one task.

Cohorts use the original first attempt, with settlement and acceptance inside the selected window. Later observations keep their dates; partial, unresolved, cancelled and refunded outcomes remain visible. Independence means accountable people or organizations, not extra agents or wallets.

Customer value compares equivalent population/period/output before installation, on first use and on recurrence: active effort, corrections, time to accepted output and unresolved work. Labor value uses the customer's measured hours and stated hourly value, less implementation and incremental provider, host, payment and support costs. Technical operation is reported separately until those customer observations exist. Public summaries use counts, methods and sanitized versions; customer files and credentials stay in their authorized workspaces.

## Delivery capacity, payment timing and sustainability

The lowest examined timely allocation is **25 engineering + eight integration/handover hours weekly**. Named availability and payment arrangements are being finalized against the actual award date. Grant and accepted commercial work use one calendar and allocate hours once.

T1's 96 engineering hours require 19.2 active days at five hours/day. Twenty to twenty-two weekdays in thirty days leave only four to fourteen engineering hours at that allocation, before holidays. Pre-award work therefore settles customer selection, access, host readiness and useful output; funded work remains prospective. Actual contributors and dates replace modeled inputs.

SCF's four payments are **$3,800 at acceptance, then $7,600, $11,400 and $15,200 after corresponding approval**. They differ from tranche delivery costs of $11,400/$11,400/$15,200. The USD-equivalent award is paid in XLM using the applicable reference on each actual payment day. A tranche completion is due within ninety calendar days of the preceding actual payment; anticipated delay is communicated before that deadline, with any extension requiring SDF's written confirmation.

The cash model assumes full package value paid in cash across work dates and no opening balance. Grant-only peak interim funding is **$17,250 / $23,275 / $26,600** at **14 / 30 / 60-day** review/payment lags. A separate proposed commercial sequence models $3,259 required, $10,960.67 with fourteen further collection-delay days, or $7,690 combined with the fourteen-day-lag grant. These are funding requirements, not available funds.

Five proposed workshares model **320 hours / $40,320 fees** and $9,560 contribution before further costs. Including the retained $200 Lutra source/compute allowance gives $9,360, or $3,280 with 20% more customer effort. Increasing both grant and customer effort 20% produces 864 hours and a $4,320 combined modeled deficit including that allowance; separate $85 core/$75 additional-engineer targets leave $5,952. The unchanged finance companion retains the dated assumptions, named scopes, original terms, eight commercial alternatives and 27 cash curves. The separate 72-hour GeoRobotix proposal needs additional capacity or a nonconflicting window. Actual opening cash, obligations and collections enter the existing forecast.

Named staff use the same package, work, invoice, cash and review records. Existing Operating plans turn the selected native packages into editable procedures with original scope, price, hours and completion measures, plus actual dates and results.

By day 150 each operator receives a source-versioned release, saved product plan/Runtime handoff, dependency/license inventory, configuration references, installation/upgrade guidance, full customer state/files, and named host, maintainer, primary/backup responder and cost owner. Updates review routes/schema/payment terms and drain admitted work before switching; rollback preserves later purchases/output. Restore reconciles operations after backup. Compatibility corrections return to maintained source with migration guidance. Customer implementation and separately scoped care sustain the reusable open-source product.
